Snap the irregular cloud onto a complete lattice g <- grid_dense_layer(sim$cloud, response = "yield", treat = "treat",                       cell_size = 9)  # Drop cells straddling a treatment boundary, keeping the lattice complete g$yield[!is.na(g$treat_purity) & g$treat_purity < 0.8] <- NA  # 2. title: Design, sample and analyse on-farm strip experiments
text: asreml-R quirks package works around, documented aren’t rediscovered hard way: summary(fit)$coef.fixed returns NULL asreml-R >= 4.2; need summary(fit, coef = TRUE)$coef.fixed. extract_fixed_effects() handles . ai.sing session-level option (asreml::asreml.options(ai.sing = TRUE)), argument asreml() — passing ai.sing = TRUE directly asreml() silently ignored. fit_integrated_joint() sets temporarily (restored exit) via ai_sing argument (default TRUE), since shared-layer random effect can trigger Average Information matrix singularities even sparse, well-behaved data. ar1(row):ar1(col) residual generally unidentifiable point-source layer joint model, handful sparse, irregularly placed observations support full spatial autocorrelation structure . fit_integrated_joint() instead uses dsum(~units | layer) (separate ..d. residual variances per layer) lets shared random effect (diag(layer) us(layer)) carry spatial information layers.

title: Design, sample and analyse on-farm strip experiments
text: sommer::mmer() defaults naMethodY = "exclude", drops row either trait missing — catastrophic , since point-source trait NA almost everywhere. fit_integrated_joint() sets naMethodY = "include" dense response keeps using rows. sommer fits treatment effect separately dense point-source traits; dense-trait estimate meaningful used (extract_fixed_effects() returns terms , named e.g. dense_response:treatB point_obs:treatB — ignore latter). sommer multi-trait model needs enough point-source observations relative grid size avoid singular system (vsr(unit, ...) fits one random-effect level per grid cell). sparse setup works fine asreml (e.g. 200 grid cells, 12 points) can fail outright sommer; denser one (e.g. 630 grid cells, 25 points) works reliably testing.

what: Fit a joint bivariate spatial model for dense and point-source data — fit_integrated_joint
title: Fit a joint bivariate spatial model for dense and point-source data — fit_integrated_joint
text: Implements "joint model" data integration strategy: rather pre-kriging point-source variable using fixed covariate (see fit_integrated_kriged()), dense response point-source measurements fitted jointly two stacked response "layers" sharing spatial random effect grid location. lets sparse point samples directly inform dense response's spatial structure (vice versa) without separate kriging step.

code: if (requireNamespace("asreml", quietly = TRUE)) {   sim <- simulate_ofe_trial(n_row = 20, n_col = 10, n_point_samples = 12, seed = 1)   fit <- fit_integrated_joint(sim$grid, sim$point_samples,                                response_dense = "dense_response",                                response_point = "point_obs")   extract_fixed_effects(fit) }  if (requireNamespace("sommer", quietly = TRUE)) {   # sommer's multi-trait model needs more point-source observations than   # asreml's to avoid a singular system; a sparser grid like the asreml   # example above is not guaranteed to converge.   sim <- simulate_ofe_trial(n_row = 30, n_col = 21, n_point_samples = 25, seed = 11)   fit <- fit_integrated_joint(sim$grid, sim$point_samples,                                response_dense = "dense_response",                                response_point = "point_obs",                                engine = "sommer")   extract_fixed_effects(fit) } #>                         term    estimate         se #> 1 dense_response:(Intercept)  0.39432617 0.04629048 #> 2      point_obs:(Intercept)  0.14632979 0.01408539 #> 3      dense_response:treatB  0.15606508 0.06546463 #> 4           point_obs:treatB -0.04129616 0.01991974 #> 5      dense_response:treatC  1.31882933 0.06546463 #> 6           point_obs:treatC -0.02382778 0.01991974
